question: For each rig and model tier, which engine and configuration produces the most completion tokens per second at the workload's concurrency (srv2 at n = 128, srv1 at n = 32) with the whole model on the card - and in particular, does ollama's never-varied slot count (OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL) close the gap to vLLM's 6,445 tok/s? Decision it feeds: the serving default per (rig, model) for the bench's r2 round - ollama at a chosen slot count, vLLM at yesterday's best cell, standalone llama-server, or LMDeploy. Rule: highest aggregate tok/s at the rig's headline n, tie broken by lower p50; a cell that spills weights to CPU or fails to launch is out. Tiers decided: 1.5B on both rigs, 7B on srv2.
arms: ollama slots: OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL in the parallel.conf drop-in, srv2 1.5B {1, 8, 128}, srv2 7B {1, 32}, srv1 1.5B {1, 32}; srv1 adds the flash-attention-off contrast (block c) with num_batch held at 1024.
llama-server standalone (ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b10481): the #18030 reproduction, batch/ubatch and -kvu arms, plus llama-batched-bench as #18030's own instrument.
LMDeploy TurboMind (openmmlab/lmdeploy:v0.16.0-cu12.8): 8 srv2 cells and 5 srv1 cells over quant-policy, cache fraction, prefix caching and the 3B checkpoint, per the 2026-08-24 dig.
vLLM control: yesterday's best cell per rig re-taken through tools/bench/serving/sweep.py; must reproduce within 10% or the rig's remaining blocks stop.
No MoE tail: block (f) was removed by the owner on 2026-08-24.

cost.estimate_note: srv2: (a) 13 + (e) 10 + (b) 16 + (d) ~40 for 8 LMDeploy cells + re-take 5 + state/restore ~30 = ~115 expected; srv1: (a)+(c) 9 + (e) 6 + (b) 7 + (d) ~35 for 5 cells + re-take 4 + ~25 = ~85. Rigs concurrent, so the campaign's wall-clock is srv2's, ~2 h; worst case (every level at the 180 s cap, F7's bound) ~5 h.
